afe file editing for AI agents: back up, validate, roll back on failure. Zero-dependency MCP server.
# ai-safe-edit

**The only safe entry point for an AI agent to edit files.**
Back up, validate, roll back on failure
— and never leave a half-broken file behind.
中文说明 · MIT · Python 3.8+ · zero dependencies
## The problem

When an agent edits a file, it writes text. When that text is assembled from
shell heredocs, regex s

ubstitutions, or model-generated code, three things go
wrong often enough to actually hurt:
| Failure | What happens |
| **Shell escaping eats characters** | A literal `\n` inside a heredoc becomes a real newline and si

lently breaks the string it was part of |
| **Regex over-matches** | A pattern meant for one line cr

osses a string boundary and corrupts neighbouring code |
| **Nested quotes** | Putting `"` inside `"
` when generating source is a syntax error — and a model produces it *often* |

The usual response is to write the lesson down. **That is not a constraint.**
The next session, or t
he next model, repeats the mistake.

> Real numbers from the project this came out of: **10 nested-quote errors in a
> single day**, all

of them landing in the actual product files, because the
> edits bypassed the tool that existed to p
revent exactly that.

> And a small confession, because it is the clearest illustration there is:
> **while writing the co

mmit message for *this repository*, the same class of
> failure hit again.** The message contained `

` `--selftest` `` inside a
> double-quoted shell string. The shell executed the backticks and delete

d the
> word. The commit went in with a sentence missing its subject — and would have
> shipped that

way, because nothing checks commit messages.
>
> Knowing about a failure mode is not protection fro
m it. Only a gate is.
## What this does
It turns the lesson into a **gate**:

1. **Back up** before touching anything → `.safe_edit_backup/<timestamp>/`
2. **Validate** immediate

ly after writing:
`.py` → `compile()` · `.json` → `json.loads` · `.yaml` → `yaml.safe_load` · `.bat`

→ ASCII-only check
3. **Roll back automatically** if validation fails, and say so
4. **Non-zero exi
t code** on failure — a model or a script cannot miss it
A half-broken file is never left behind.

## Use it from an AI agent (MCP)

`mcp_server.py` exposes it over MCP — stdio, JSON-RPC 2.0, **no dependencies to
install**. Tools: `s
afe_edit`, `edit_check`, `edit_rollback`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Works with any MCP client — including **DeepSeek Harness**, Claude Code, Cursor
and others.
## Why an agent should be forced through this

An agent that can write files freely will, eventually, write a broken one. The
question is whether t

hat failure surfaces **immediately, with a rollback**, or
**later, as a mysterious error in a file n
obody remembers touching**.
This project's answer, learned the hard way:

- **A lesson written down is not a constraint.** A lesson turned into a gate is.
- **The caller must

be told when it failed.** Silent success is worse than loud
failure — an agent that thinks its edit
landed will build on top of it.
## Honest limits

- It **cannot** judge whether an edit is *correct* — only that the result still
parses. Semantic cor

rectness still needs tests, gates, and a human.
- It does **not prevent** a bypass. If you want bypa

sses to at least leave a
trace, see the companion idea below.
- `.py` / `.json` / `.yaml` / `.bat` a

re the validated formats today. Other
extensions are backed up and written, but not checked.
## Related work

This tool was built independently inside a hardware-design agent project. After
it was working, we r

ead **DeepSeek Harness**'s source and found it solves the
same class of problem from the other end:

*hardening an experiment requires
explicit user approval* (`install_bundle` + `pendingBuilds`), so n

othing the
model writes reaches persistent configuration without a human.
The two are complementary:
| | DeepSeek Harness | ai-safe-edit |
| Approach | **Prevent** — a change needs approval before it persists | **Contain** — a change is va

lidated and rolled back if it breaks |
| Strength | Nothing unauthorized gets written | Nothing brok
en survives, even unauthorized edits |

A companion idea in the same spirit: after every successful edit, record a hash
of the file. A check

er can then compare the current hash against the last record
and flag **"this file was changed witho

ut going through the tool"** — turning a
silent bypass into a visible one.
